observations.title: Go and WHATWG parsers differ on noncanonical port forms
observations.detail: Go requires a nonempty literal Port without numeric range checking. WHATWG removes default :80 and rejects >65535. Thus not all syntactically noncanonical discovery URLs have identical acceptance. Desktop managed Core uses 127.0.0.1:0 and emits a valid assigned port, so the publisher does not create these records in the reviewed product path. CLI remains loopback-only; no credential, management or writer authority is granted. Invalid ports fail at HTTP use.
observations.follow_up: If supporting externally authored shared discovery, define one canonical port policy and add default/out-of-range vectors. Do not claim full URL parser equivalence.

verified: All 11 current source SHA256 values exactly match frozen manifest, and manifest/author-summary hashes match the supplied freeze.
CLI uses explicit nonempty RESEARCHOS_CLI_DISCOVERY before an existing legacy cwd file; invalid explicit or legacy records return errors without shared fallback.
hostDiscovery, doctorReport and cliHostInstanceID use the same resolver. Native identity compares URL/PID/dataDir and retains the pre-existing native pipe/session credential flow.
Shared locator and shared discovery enforce exact four-key JSON with duplicate detection, bounded bytes, absolute local canonical paths, matching stable Host ID/data root and loopback HTTP.

Publication checks OWNED READY, manager-bound paths and currentHost twice before global paths; complete temporary file is fsynced and published via exclusive hard link. Existing malformed or conflicting bytes are never replaced.
Development launcher overrides RESEARCHOS_SHARED_HOST_LOCATOR_DISABLED=1; disabled publisher returns before any fs access. Source tests use explicit temporary LOCALAPPDATA and fixture directories.
Protected manager/native/IPC/verbs/control-discovery/identity/domain protocol paths independently have zero diff against HEAD; EXTERNAL_HOST_PRESENT still rejects live external processes.

Stable Host.InstanceID derives directory plus stable SID reference, so same directory string/principal permits PID and URL changes without modifying locator. Changing root string or principal remains conflict.

build-validator.py recursively copies the complete main/preload directories; build-development.py copies those staged directories, so tracked helper is included. A new development build was not performed.
limits: Source review only; parent verifier separately reruns approved Go and Node fixtures. Author fixture results are not independent execution evidence here.
No product/Electron/Core/native process, provider/model call, actual user AppData, database migration or formal acceptance was exercised.

Current uncommitted candidate lies outside development-builder dirty allowlist; the normal builder requires integration/commit before rebuilding. No built desktop artifact is asserted to contain this patch yet.
Multiple roots, different stable identity, corrupted locator and filesystems without hard-link support remain explicit blocked recovery situations; no automatic reconciliation.
Same-user local races are not a protected agent isolation boundary; locator remains a nonsecret hint and existing native authentication is unchanged.
